item.description:

ABNT20 KNHC 251718
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located about 160 miles east of the southernmost Cabo
Verde Islands, and on Tropical Storm Fay, located well to the
west-southwest of the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT2.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Reinhart

...FAY WEAKENS OVER THE ATLANTIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.8N 43.0W
ABOUT 1075 MI...1730 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 250 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 43.0 West. Fay is moving 
toward the west-southwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A gradual turn to the 
southwest is expected to occur along with an increase in forward 
speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds have weakened to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Gradual weakening is expected to occur for the next 
few days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 251437
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Convection continues to increase mostly on the northern side of 
Fay, while resisting dry air entrainment based as displayed on the 
visible and water vapor imagery. The lastest TAFB Dvorak fix came in 
at T2.5/45 kt, however a recent SAR pass found peak winds around 55 
kt. In addition, the objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS are 
in the range of 37-42 kt. A recent ASCAT pass showed that some of 
the peak wind vectors were around 40 kt, but given the small size 
of Fay, it is possible that the ASCAT is undersampling the peak 
winds. Based on a compromise of all the available data, the initial 
intensity is raised to 50 kt for this advisory. 
 
Additional strengthening is still possible over the next several 
hours, as Fay is in a region of weak deep-layer shear and 
marginally favorable thermodynamic conditions. The statistical 
GFS/ECMWF SHIPS intensity guidance indicates that northerly wind 
shear will increase tonight, which should help force dry air 
into the cyclone. Therefore, Fay should gradually weaken through 
the period, and degenerate into a post-tropical cyclone during the 
weekend. The current NHC intensity forecast is in good agreement 
with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
Fay's initial motion is estimated to be due west, or 275/3 kt and is 
steered by a subtropical ridge anchored over the central Atlantic. 
The initial position for Fay has been adjusted to the left of the 
previous advisory and the center of the cyclone appears to have 
reformed to the northeast.  By Saturday, a gradual turn toward the 
west-southwest and southwest is forecast while Fay weakens and 
become a vertically shallow remnant low steered by the low-level 
flow. The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one 
and lies close to the GDMI ensemble mean and the HCCA corrected 
consensus aid.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 3a
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT32 KNHC 251748
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Intermediate Advisory Number 3A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
500 PM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
...CENTER OF GONZALO NEARING THE EASTERN CABO VERDE ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM CVT...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 22.7W
ABOUT 70 MI...115 KM S OF SAL CABO VERDE
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The Cabo Verde Islands
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM CVT (1800 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was 
located near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 22.7 West. Gonzalo is 
moving toward the north near 10 mph (17 km/h). A northward to 
north-northwestward motion is expected through tonight, followed by 
a slower north-northwestward motion over the weekend. On the 
forecast track, the center will pass near or over the eastern 
portions of the Cabo Verde Islands later today and tonight.  
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher
gusts. Little change in strength is expected today. A gradual 
weakening trend is forecast to begin tonight and continue through 
the weekend. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
primary to the northeast of the center. The official observing 
station on Sal in the Cabo Verde Islands recently reported a 
sustained wind of 35 mph (56 km/h) with a gust to 48 mph (78 km/h).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Gonzalo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT2 and WMO header WTNT42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions will continue over portions of 
the Cabo Verde Islands through tonight.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Storm Gonzalo is expected to produce rainfall
totals of 1 to 3 inches (25 to 75 mm) across the eastern portions of
the islands of Cabo Verde on Friday and Saturday with less than 1
inch anticipated for the western side of the island chain. Heavy
rain along the coastal areas of Guinea-Bissau, Gambia, and Senegal
will produce totals between 2 to 4 inches (50 to 100 mm) with
isolated higher amounts along the immediate coast.
 
SURF: Swells generated by the storm are expected to affect the Cabo
Verde Islands through Saturday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT42 KNHC 251445
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 PM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Gonzalo remains a sheared tropical cyclone with the deep convection 
located northeast of the elongated center.  ASCAT data from around 
1100 UTC revealed a large area of tropical-storm force winds 
located over the northeastern portion of the circulation with peak 
winds of around 45 kt.  Those peak winds were the basis for 
increasing the intensity to 45 kt on the 1200 UTC intermediate 
advisory, and the initial intensity for this advisory remains 
unchanged.

The initial motion estimate is north-northwest or 345/9 kt. A 
mid-level trough over the eastern Atlantic is expected to steer 
Gonzalo north-northwestward to northward today with the center 
passing near or over the easternmost Cabo Verde Islands. A 
north-northwestward heading should then continue over the weekend 
with some reduction in forward speed as the system weakens and 
becomes more vertically shallow.  The updated NHC track forecast is 
similar to the previous advisory and lies closest to the HFIP 
corrected consensus aid. 

Little change in strength is expected today as Gonzalo passes near 
or over the Cabo Verde Islands.  The shear is forecast to increase 
to more than 30 kt later tonight and become even more belligerent 
over the weekend.  This should cause weakening to begin by Saturday 
morning with a continued gradual spin down through the weekend.  As 
the SSTs cool along the track and strong shear continues, the 
system is likely to lose organized deep convection by late Sunday 
or Sunday night and become post-tropical. The NHC intensity 
forecast is close to a blend of the Google Deep Mind and HFIP 
corrected consensus aids. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions will continue across portions of the 
Cabo Verde Islands into tonight. 
 
2. Heavy rains from Gonzalo could affect the eastern portions of 
the Cabo Verde Islands and the western coast of Africa between 
Guinea-Bissau to Senegal through Saturday. Areas of flash flooding 
will be possible along the Africa coasts with some isolated flash 
flood concerns for the eastern portions of Cabo Verde.
